parts.visual:
A massive shift in global economics: Companies stopped selling you software for $100 once, and started charging you $10 a month forever. This is SaaS.

The SaaS Holy Trinity:
1. MRR (Monthly Recurring Revenue): The guaranteed money arriving every single month.
2. CAC (Customer Acquisition Cost): How much money you spend on marketing to get one new subscriber.
3. LTV (Lifetime Value): How much total money that subscriber will pay you before they cancel.
parts.audio: In the Subscription Economy, companies don't sell products; they rent them forever. This model relies on three metrics: Monthly Recurring Revenue, Customer Acquisition Cost, and Lifetime Value.

questions.question: A software company spends $50 in advertising to get one new user (CAC = $50). The user pays $10 a month. They cancel after 3 months (LTV = $30). What is the result?
options: The company is bleeding cash. Their Customer Acquisition Cost ($50) is higher than the Customer Lifetime Value ($30). The business model is fundamentally broken.
The company should spend more on ads.
questions.correct_answer: The company is bleeding cash. Their Customer Acquisition Cost ($50) is higher than the Customer Lifetime Value ($30). The business model is fundamentally broken.
questions.explanation: In SaaS, if your LTV is not at least 3 times higher than your CAC, your company will eventually die.

questions.question: Listen to the CEO's ultimate fear. What metric is destroying the company?
questions.tts_text: We signed up 10,000 new users this month, which is great. But 12,000 of our old users canceled their subscriptions. We are shrinking.
questions.explanation: Churn (cancellations) is the silent killer of subscription companies. It is a leaky bucket; you cannot pour water in fast enough if the hole at the bottom is too big.

questions.question: Why do Wall Street investors love 'SaaS' (Software as a Service) companies so much?
options: Because 'Recurring Revenue' is highly predictable. Investors hate uncertainty. A company guaranteed to make $10M next month is worth far more than a company that *might* sell $10M of hardware.
Because the software is fun to use.
questions.correct_answer: Because 'Recurring Revenue' is highly predictable. Investors hate uncertainty. A company guaranteed to make $10M next month is worth far more than a company that *might* sell $10M of hardware.
questions.explanation: This predictability is why SaaS companies are valued at incredibly high multiples compared to traditional retail companies.

questions.question: What is 'Freemium'?
options: A pricing strategy where the basic product is provided free of charge, but money is charged for additional features, services, or virtual goods.
questions.correct_answer: A pricing strategy where the basic product is provided free of charge, but money is charged for additional features, services, or virtual goods.
questions.explanation: Freemium is an aggressive tactic to lower Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) by letting the product market itself.
